name: rotor-bistab
note: THE BISTABILITY PROBE. R39-rotor 1c found that a quiet hover equilibrium and a +/-50 deg rail-to-rail yaw limit cycle COEXIST on the same airframe at the same condition, and that roughly 8 deg of disturbance selects between them: rec384 entered the hover segment at azErr -0.1 deg and held rms 0.01 for 25 s, while rec387 - byte-identical card, same airframe, same replicate index, both at 6 m/s and ~2160 m - entered at -7.9 deg and spent the segment railed at +/-50 deg. The cycle also survives removal of the stimulus. That is a disturbance-amplitude threshold and nothing in the corpus measures it. DESIGN: quiet at boresight, then three kicks of INCREASING amplitude with a return to boresight after each, so every replicate delivers six disturbances (+5, -5, +8, -8, +12, -12) and the recovery legs both re-arm the next test and measure whether the cycle self-clears. The steps are ABSOLUTE azimuths from the run anchor, so the disturbance entering hoverstep8 is 8 deg from quiet and not 3 deg from the previous hold - that is why each step is bracketed by a return rather than chained. 30 s of hold is 3.3-5.5 periods of the measured 0.11-0.19 Hz mode: enough to see a cycle persist, NOT enough for osc_mode's four-period evidence rule, so expect wobbleFreqHz* to stay NULL here. The discriminating readouts are terminal |azErr|, stickRailPctY and wobbleCoherenceAzErr, not the frequency; rotor-hover's 50 s yaw legs are where the frequency gets measured. PASS: every hoverrec* segment returns to and holds under 1 deg of |azErr|, and stickRailPctY is under 10% on all six scored steps, on all three airframes. FAIL: one kick drops the aircraft into a sustained cycle that is STILL RUNNING at the end of the following hoverrec* - stickRailPctY > 40% carried across a segment boundary is the signature, and the smallest kick that does it is the threshold this card exists to find. The phenomenon is stochastic, so read the 4 replicates x 3 airframes as twelve independent draws and never as one averaged cell. ENTRY IS A REAL HOVER: startSpeed 0 is DECLARED, not absent - since v1.0.0 the harness places the aircraft at 0 m/s at startAlt and calls ChaseController.Forget every replicate, instead of reading the 0 as 'unset' and spawning at DroneSpawnSpeed. That per-replicate reset is what makes the twelve draws independent; the 48 R39 captures had none (no '# entry' header on any of them) and their replicates were a monotone drift, not a sample. The airframe list names the three rotorcraft outright - left empty it fell through to Drone/DroneAirframe (a fixed-wing jet) and cls then refused the card on every lane. A tiltwing/VTOL must already be in the HOVER configuration (a card never writes customAxis1). THE COLLECTIVE IS NOT OWNED BY THIS CARD AND CANNOT BE: ScenarioPlayer.OwnInputs returns early at EntrySpeed <= 0 by deliberate design (its 'declared-zero-ok' comment - a fixed throttle at zero airspeed is a climb, not a trim), so ci.throttle keeps the last value the built-in level-hold wrote, TestDrone.HoldThrottle = 0.60, for the whole card. Expect a slow CLIMB and read positionRMSM / driftRateMS as containing that vertical component. Not fixable from a card file: a config pin on Scenario/ScenarioThrottle is read AFTER the early return, so it would do nothing. startAlt 2500 m, for two reasons: it is a hover altitude R39 already proved flyable (rotorcraft reached 2761 m), and it survives the operator forgetting Drone/DroneAltDeckM - at the 3000 default the decks land at 1000 and 4000 m, both above the 500 m card floor, so the batch is degraded rather than lost. SET Drone/DroneAltDeckM = 0 ANYWAY: with a 3-key roster the Latin-square diagonal puts lanes 0 and 2 low and lane 1 high, i.e. one airframe at a different air density from the other two. count 6 over the 3-key list = TWO LANES PER AIRFRAME, wrapping. It costs no wall clock (lanes fly concurrently) and it buys two things this card specifically needs: EIGHT independent draws per airframe instead of four, on a phenomenon that is stochastic by definition; and insurance against task #85, since R40 lost 1 lane in 10 to a placement velocity blow-up, which is a FATAL abort that takes the lane's remaining replicates with it and would delete a whole airframe from the answer. R42 VERDICT (v1.0.1, shipped 60/20): the card still has NOT measured the disturbance threshold it exists to find, and the reason changed. In R41 it measured a config artifact -- a monotone speed divergence on AttackHelo1, retracted as LAW-LEDGER.md X29. In R42 AttackHelo1 converges (fixedWindowOffDeg down 85-95%: hoverstep8 15.33->2.31, hoverstep12 25.81->1.32, hoverrec8 18.61->1.76, hoverrec12 23.76->1.69; pedal rail 66.1%->0.0%) but converges to a DETERMINISTIC 1.5-2.4 deg standing residual at replicate CV +/-1-3% -- so it FAILS this card's own PASS bar (every hoverrec* under 1 deg) on 3 of 3 recovery legs. That residual is ledger H7 and is the first above-floor rotorcraft pointing measurement in the corpus; L15 is the candidate mechanism. THE BISTABILITY QUESTION IS STILL BLOCKED ON THE COLLECTIVE (H5): AttackHelo1 accelerates 4.5 -> 38 m/s across the card and never returns, so every later segment is a different flight condition and none of them is a hover -- the twelve draws are not exchangeable. QuadVTOL1 is the only airframe hovering here and it reproduces R41 exactly. BEFORE RE-FLYING: give this card an armToggle. H7 cannot be turned into an experiment without one, and its absence is also why R42 could not exercise the v1.0.1 arm=-1 fix (ledger O14). repeat wants 4k+1.
